definition: A character's body does not translate in a direction until its weight has left the base of support in that direction; lifting the free foot while the centre of mass still sits fully over the support foot produces almost no displacement, while a fast weight shift off the support foot produces near-immediate falling motion in that direction.
purpose: Explain, mechanically, why a locomotion or travel action costs a variable number of setup frames before real displacement begins, and name the lever an animator actually controls: the STARTING POSE's own weight position.
visible_effect: A character posed with weight already shifted toward its direction of travel begins visibly displacing within very few frames of the first key; a character posed with weight centred or on the opposite foot spends several frames leaning and shifting before the same displacement begins, even for what is nominally the same action.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: A character that should read as already ready to go but is posed weight-centred reads as sluggish or hesitant to start, independent of how the rest of the motion is timed; the opposite mismatch (already weight-shifted when the shot wants a calm, uncommitted stance) reads as unintended urgency or a held-back lean.
physical_interpretation: The body's centre of mass must exit the convex hull of its current base of support before unsupported translation (falling into the direction of travel) begins; with weight fully committed to one foot, lifting the other foot changes nothing about the support relationship and so produces no meaningful centre-of-mass displacement.
use_cases: posing a character's first key for a shot with a stated urgency (a fast getaway, a reactive dodge) so it can begin travelling within very few frames
diagnosing a walk or run cycle's first step reading as slow to start, by checking whether the starting pose already had weight shifted toward the direction of travel
a blocking pass choosing between a relaxed/centred silhouette and a ready/weight-shifted one, based on how many frames the shot can spend before real motion must be visible
non_use_cases: a character already mid-stride or mid-travel — this concerns only the first step out of a static pose, not steady-state locomotion
non-physical or deliberately weightless motion (flight, teleport-style game abilities, ghosts) where no base-of-support relationship is being modelled at all
an action that does not require full-body translation (a punch, a gesture) where the mechanism this entry names does not gate the action's onset
interactions: structural_understanding — that card's balance measurement (`ai/pose.js measurePose`, MOT-011) is a SINGLE-FRAME snapshot of whether the centre of mass sits inside a declared support polygon; this entry is about the same measurement's CHANGE across a startup phase (the frame at which it would flip from supported to unsupported), which nothing currently samples across a range the way `sampleMotion` samples velocity

startup_frame_budget (W01, video 2) — that card treats startup frame count as a general design dial for how reactable an action feels; this entry names one concrete physical mechanism (weight has to leave the support base) that is a real driver of that count specifically for travel-initiating actions, not a restatement of it

weight_then_strength_formula (W02, video 19) — a different beat of the same weight-is-shown-not-stated family: that card is a struggle-then-release timing signature for a heavy lift, this one is the frame cost of leaving a stance, both readable from how weight visibly moves before the main action
cadence_representation: Not computed anywhere. The two measurements this would join both exist individually — `ai/pose.js measurePose`'s `balance`/`centre_of_mass` at a single declared-support frame, and `ai/motion.js sampleMotion`'s per-frame `position`/`linear_velocity` series — but nothing currently calls `measurePose` across a frame RANGE the way `sampleMotion` samples motion, so there is no existing way to ask "at which frame did the declared support relationship stop holding."
control_surface: `compile_pose` / `author_motion` return a single frame's balance when support is declared; `sample_motion` (the MCP tool over `ai/motion.js sampleMotion`) already returns `position` and `linear_velocity` series that could detect the ONSET half (when displacement actually starts) without any new code — nothing currently joins that onset frame back to the starting pose's balance state.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Onset half — real today: `ai/motion.js sampleMotion`'s `position` and `linear_velocity` series can report the first frame after an action's start key where `linear_velocity` departs meaningfully from near-zero, a literal frame count for how long until real displacement begins. Support half — real but single-frame: `ai/pose.js measurePose`'s `balance` reports whether the centre-of-mass proxy is inside a DECLARED support polygon at one frame; sampling it at the first key alone would say whether the character starts already unsupported toward its direction of travel. Joining the two — does the onset frame arrive sooner when the starting balance is already unsupported toward the travel direction — is not built.
generation_or_modification_methods: None. No strategy in `ai/plan.js` or `authorMotion` currently derives a starting pose's weight position from a declared urgency or a target onset-frame count.
failure_modes: posing a character weight-centred at the first key of a shot that needs an immediate fast start, costing several unplanned frames of lean-and-shift before real travel begins
posing a character already weight-shifted for a shot meant to read as calm or uncommitted, which reads as an unintended lean or held-back urgency
judging a walk cycle's startup as "the timing is wrong" when the actual cause is the starting pose's weight position, not the spacing of the keys that follow it
roblox_considerations: None beyond the shared Motor6D rig/root-part model already used by `ai/pose.js measurePose` and `ai/motion.js sampleMotion` — the mechanism is rig-independent.
examples: presenter stands with weight fully on one foot and lifts the other: "pretty much nothing happens, I don't go anywhere, because my whole weight is on this one" — video @ 01:51-02:03
presenter switches weight off the support foot fast: "I start falling... quite rapidly into going that way" — video @ 02:04-02:16

the stated shot-planning consequence: pose the character weight-shifted toward the door for an immediate fast start ("I can go okay and just get going right away"), versus a centred pose that costs "more time, more frames" of lean-and-shift first — video @ 02:19-03:00
